1. Core Clinical Tension: A 43-year-old woman with a history of rheumatic multivalvular heart disease and mechanical mitral-aortic valve replacements presented with progressive right-sided heart failure. While prosthetic valve failure or recurrent rheumatic valve disease was immediately suspected, multimodality cardiovascular imaging revealed an extremely rare multicystic, septated constrictive pericardial lesion mimicking hydatid disease or cystic neoplastic disease in the absence of active pulmonary parenchymal or nodal lesions.

2. Admission Breakpoint: Admission triage terminates after clinical evaluation, transthoracic echocardiography, chest CT, and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) documenting preserved mechanical prosthetic function and multicystic constrictive pericarditis. Invasive pericardial tissue biopsy, microbiological testing, and surgical pericardiectomy define the post-triage confirmatory stage.

3. Differential Distinctions: Prosthetic valve malfunction or paravalvular leak was excluded by normal echocardiographic prosthetic Doppler parameters and preserved biventricular contractility. Echinococcal (hydatid) cyst or congenital pericardial cysts were ruled out by pericardial biopsy demonstrating chronic granulomatous inflammation and identification of mycobacterial bacilli, confirming tuberculous constrictive pericarditis.
case_prompt:
A 43-year-old woman presented with a 3-month history of progressive fatigue, peripheral edema, abdominal distention, and worsening clinical signs of right-sided heart failure. Her past medical history was notable for severe rheumatic mitral, aortic, and tricuspid polyvalvulopathy, for which she had undergone double mechanical mitral and aortic valve replacements along with tricuspid ring annuloplasty four years previously. Two years prior to presentation, she had completed treatment for chronic cervical lymphadenitis.

On physical examination, the patient had signs of systemic venous congestion, including jugular venous distention, tender hepatomegaly, and bilateral lower-extremity pitting edema. Mechanical prosthetic heart valve clicks were crisp and regular, without pathologic murmurs.

Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated preserved left and right ventricular systolic function, normal seating and leaflet motion of both mechanical prostheses with physiologic transvalvular gradients, and an intact tricuspid annuloplasty ring. However, there was a markedly thickened pericardium filled with multiple loculated cystic structures associated with respiratory-dependent ventricular septal shifting and signs of impaired diastolic filling (adiastole). A contrast-enhanced thoracic computed tomography (CT) scan revealed an abundant, septated, multicystic pericardial effusion without evidence of pulmonary parenchymal infiltrates or mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) confirmed severe pericardial constriction by numerous pericardial cysts displaying intermediate signal intensity on T2-weighted black-blood spin-echo sequences and marked hyperintensity on T2-weighted STIR sequences, accompanied by diffuse pericardial thickening.

A 43-year-old woman presented with a 3-month history of progressive fatigue, peripheral edema, abdominal distention, and worsening clinical signs of right-sided heart failure. Her past medical history was notable for severe rheumatic multivalvular heart disease, for which she had undergone mechanical double mitral and aortic valve replacements along with tricuspid annuloplasty four years previously. Two years prior to presentation, she had completed treatment for chronic cervical lymphadenitis.

On physical examination, the patient showed signs of systemic venous congestion, including jugular venous distention, tender hepatomegaly, and bilateral lower-extremity pitting edema. Mechanical prosthetic valve clicks were crisp and regular, without pathologic murmurs.

Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated preserved left and right ventricular systolic function, normal seating and motion of both mechanical prostheses with physiologic gradients, and an intact tricuspid ring. However, there was a markedly thickened pericardium containing multiple loculated cystic collections associated with diastolic septal bounce and signs of impaired diastolic filling (adiastole). Contrast-enhanced thoracic CT demonstrated an abundant, septated, multicystic pericardial effusion without active pulmonary parenchymal infiltrates or mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Cardiac MRI confirmed features of pericardial constriction caused by numerous pericardial cysts with intermediate T2 black-blood signal, intense STIR hyperintensity, and prominent pericardial thickening.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: In a patient with prior double mechanical valve replacement presenting with new-onset right heart failure, prosthetic valve thrombosis, pannus ingrowth, or paravalvular regurgitation were the leading clinical suspects; however, echocardiography verified normal prosthetic hemodynamics, intact seating, and preserved biventricular systolic performance.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Transthoracic echocardiography showed good functioning of the mitral and aortic prostheses, as well as of the tricuspid ring, and good ventricular systolic function

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Pericardial Echinococcosis (Hydatid Cyst) / Benign Multicystic Pericardial Malformation
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The striking radiological finding of an abundant, septated, multicystic pericardial effusion causing constriction mimicked pericardial hydatid disease or congenital multicystic mesothelial proliferation; however, tissue histology revealed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation rather than laminated parasitic cyst walls or benign epithelium.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: A thoracic CT-scan showed abundant septated pericardial effusion, mullticystic, but without involvement of the pulmonary or ganglion parenchymas (B).

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Due to persistent adiastole, pericardial tissue biopsy and subsequent surgical pericardial decortication were performed; histopathological analysis and microbiological testing demonstrated a chronic granulomatous reaction positive for Koch's bacillus, definitively confirming multicystic tuberculous pericarditis.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: A pericardial biopsy was carried out, which found a granulomatous inflammatory reaction with positive finding for BK virus.

editor_comments: Standardized admission diagnostic case following Stanford MedCaseReasoning methodology. Admission presentation strictly includes clinical exam, TTE, chest CT, and cardiac MRI, while withholding invasive pericardial biopsy, histopathology, microbiological results, and operative pericardial decortication.
